kind: DSH Session Query feasibility audit — measured, not assumed

dshImplementation.verifiedBy: reading each package.json `version` field on disk
dshImplementation.note: The ruling named source paths under `packages/**`. This deployment ships BUILT packages, so the equivalent inspected sources are the published `lib/types/*.d.ts` declaration files and `README.md` of each package above. The declarations are the same public surface the TypeScript sources compile to.

verdictDetail: A supported first-party persistence reader (`readColdSessionLog` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-query`) can inspect explicitly identified Session logs from the external Palimpsest process, WITHOUT resuming or activating an Agent and WITHOUT a model call. Measured end to end.

requiredMapping.producerToSessionIdentity: The DSH agent loop (`dsh-agent-loop`) appends events to a Session; the Session's identity is the `SessionHeader.id` (SessionId), persisted in the header frame of the session's own generation file.
requiredMapping.sessionIdentityToStorageQueryOwner: Storage is owned by `ctx.sessionPersistence`, provided by the mounted backend `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` (`JsonlSessionPersistence`, `readonly name = 'session-persistence-jsonl'`). The query surface is `ctx.sessionQuery` (`SessionQueryEngine`, provided by `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-query` with the sqlite backend mounted).
requiredMapping.supportedReadInterface: `readColdSessionLog(persistence, sessionId, signal?)` — an EXPORTED STANDALONE FUNCTION in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-query` (declared in `lib/types/cold-read.d.ts`). It takes a `SessionPersistence` directly, so it does NOT require the full DSH host context. Also available: `SessionQueryEngine.readSession/listEvents/readEvent/readSurface/traceSession` when a query service is composed.
requiredMapping.palimpsestConsumer: The external Palimpsest process mounts `JsonlSessionPersistence` in a bare Cordis `Context` and calls `readColdSessionLog` — measured working.
requiredMapping.missingEdge: There is NO producer that binds a canonical Work AttemptId to a DSH SessionId. See `attempt-session-binding` below.

reachabilityMeasurements.how: Absolute `file://` ESM import of `~/.dsh/profiles/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/<pkg>/lib/index.js`. Palimpsest's own `node_modules` contains no `@deepseek-ai/*`, so the profile path is the only route.
reachabilityMeasurements.mountDetail: `new Context()` then `await ctx.plugin(JsonlSessionPersistence, { root, compression: 'zstd' })` yields `ctx.sessionPersistence`. Measured: no DSH host, no agent, no provider.
reachabilityMeasurements.listDetail: `ctx.sessionPersistence.list()` returned 1142 session records; each record carries `{ header, revision, sizeBytes }`.
reachabilityMeasurements.readDetail: `readColdSessionLog(sp, SessionId('session-2a47953a-c184-4797-89fb-2872da37e0a7'))` returned a 75-event log: header.version 4, isSeeded false, inheritedEventCount 0, cwd present.
reachabilityMeasurements.readActivationDetail: No `ctx.sessions` store was mounted, and the read path is documented as never making a session live; measured live-session count after two reads: no session store mounted.
reachabilityMeasurements.readOnlyDetail: The generation file's mtime, size and sha256 were byte-identical before and after two reads.
reachabilityMeasurements.determinismDetail: Two reads produced identical (seq, type) projections.
reachabilityMeasurements.postExitDetail: The measured session belongs to a host process that is not the current process, and it read successfully from disk — i.e. the read is a pure storage read.
reachabilityMeasurements.whichSessionIdIdentifiesTheExecutedAgent: `SessionHeader.id`. The measured header also carries `cwd`, `createdAt`, `isSeeded`, `delegationDepth`, and optional `parentSession` / `origin` / `agentPreset`.
reachabilityMeasurements.howSessionIdBecomesAvailableToPalimpsest: NOT ESTABLISHED. See the missing-edge finding below.
reachabilityMeasurements.howCallerIsRestrictedToTheRelevantAttemp: NOT ESTABLISHED — there is no Work Attempt binding to restrict against, so V0 must restrict by an explicitly supplied SessionId plus an explicit header/scope check, and must refuse rather than guess.

missingEdgeFinding.statement: No component writes a durable, canonical binding from a Work AttemptId to a DSH SessionId.
evidence: The worker port spawns DSH with `cwd: runInput.workDir` (src/deployment/work_worker.ts:756) and never records the child's SessionId.

A scan of all 1142 persisted session headers found 462 with a path containing `palimpsest`, but ZERO whose cwd is a `.palimpsest/worlds/<attemptId>` execution world. The observed palimpsest cwds are host directories (e.g. `C:\Users\66494\.dsh\palimpsest-dogfood\real-host`).

G1-B's artifact locator can PARSE an AttemptId out of a worker session path (`worker-<uuid>/session.v4.jsonl.zstd` under a `-worlds-` slug), but it is a research-scope locator, not a canonical producer, and no such artifact exists in this deployment.
The DSH `SessionHeader` carries `cwd` and optional `parentSession`/`origin`, but no Work AttemptId field.
missingEdgeFinding.consequenceForV0: The execution view must report SESSION_UNBOUND for real product attempts, and must refuse a caller-supplied SessionId as binding authority. The controlled fixture path is therefore required to exercise the reader.
missingEdgeFinding.smallestFutureIntegration: The worker port would record the DSH SessionId it observes (or the session file path it created) into a durable, Attempt-keyed record — a host-lifecycle binding, not a new canonical owner. Not implemented in V0 per §11.

callerAuthorizationBoundary.v0Constraint: V0 exposes NO generic `listSessions()` surface. A caller must supply an explicit SessionId, and the reader refuses unless the supplied id resolves to a header whose immutable identity matches the request. No mtime selection, no directory-similarity search, no scanning of personal histories.

eventVocabulary.envelope: { type, seq, time, data } plus an optional `ignorable: true` marker; surface events additionally carry `surfaceOp` and `sourceEventSeqs`
eventVocabulary.turnEndReasons: A closed union (`TurnEndReasonMap`) including `completed`, `aborted`, `blocked` — so a turn/end is NOT a success signal by itself.
eventVocabulary.unknownTypeHandling: A type outside KNOWN_SESSION_EVENT_TYPES without `ignorable: true` MUST cause the reader to refuse the log rather than silently drop it. V0 preserves this: an unrecognised REQUIRED event is a read failure, not an empty stream.

v0Returns: duration only when real timing exists
sensitiveContent.rawInspection: deferred to a future separately-authorized capability

sourceLocations.conclusion: readColdSessionLog is an exported standalone function taking a SessionPersistence
ctx.sessionQuery is the unified query service with readSession/listEvents/readEvent/readSurface/traceSession
the persistence backend registers as ctx.sessionPersistence and requires a root directory
SessionEvent envelope is { type, seq, time, data } with an optional ignorable marker
the worker port spawns DSH with cwd = the execution world and records no SessionId
the G1-B locator can parse an AttemptId from a worker session path, but no such artifact exists here
